introduction_markdown:
This paper is arranged in three sections, A, B and C. Section A: answer ALL 5 questions; you will be graded for the best 4 answers. Section B: answer ALL 2 questions in this section. Section C: answer 2 questions out of 3; if you attempt more than 2 questions, only the first two will be considered. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Calculators are allowed. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

**Useful data:** relative atomic masses H = 1.0, C = 12.0, O = 16.0, N = 14.0; 1 faraday = 96000 coulombs; molar volume of a gas at r.t.p. = 24000 cm$^3$; specific heat capacity of water = 4.2 J g$^{-1}$ $^\circ$C$^{-1}$; Avogadro number = $6.02\times10^{23}$; $0^\circ$C = 273 K.
enonce_intro_markdown:
A student was provided with three salts, **X**, **Y** and **Z** alongside with some laboratory equipment and the following reagents; Aqueous sodium hydroxide, ($\mathrm{NaOH_{(aq)}}$), Aqueous Barium chloride, ($\mathrm{BaCl_{2(aq)}}$), Dilute $\mathrm{HCl_{(aq)}}$

A series of tests were carried out as shown on the following table. Study and complete the table.

| | TEST PROCEDURE | OBSERVATION | CONCLUSION |
|---|---|---|---|
| a. i) | To 2 cm$^3$ of solution **X** is added 5 drops of $\mathrm{NaOH_{(aq)}}$ and warmed | A colourless pungent gas is evolved that turns damp red litmus paper blue. | ......... *[2 marks]* |
| a. ii) | A sample of **X** is strongly heated in a test tube | A brown gas is evolved. | ......... *[2 marks]* |
| b. i) | To 2 cm$^3$ of a solution of **Y**, is added 2 drops of $\mathrm{NaOH_{(aq)}}$ | ......... | $\mathrm{Fe^{2+}}$ ions present *[1 mark]* |
| b. ii) | To 2 cm$^3$ of a solution of **Y**, is added 2 drops of $\mathrm{BaCl_{2(aq)}}$ followed by dil HCl | ......... | $\mathrm{SO_3^{2-}}$ ions present *[2 marks]* |
| c. i) | ......... | **Z** gives a brick red flame colour | ......... *[3 marks]* |
| c. ii) | To 2 cm$^3$ of a solution of **Z**, is added 5 drops of dil HCl without heating | A gas is evolved which turns lime water milky. | ......... *[2 marks]* |
incertitudes: Points imprimés par ligne du tableau : a.i 2, a.ii 2, b.i 1, b.ii 2, c.i 3, c.ii 2, puis (d) 3, (e) 3, (f) 2 ; regroupés par lettre (a) 4, (b) 3, (c) 5, (d) 3, (e) 3, (f) 2 ; total 20, conforme.

6 : le tableau d'essais du sujet est recopié en entier dans l'énoncé de l'exercice et les cases à compléter sont reprises dans chaque sous-question. 6(d) : Y = sulfite de fer(II) et Z = carbonate de calcium sont des sels insolubles alors que le sujet parle de « solution » ; la réponse attendue est celle déduite des ions de la conclusion imprimée (SO3 2- et Fe2+ pour Y ; Ca2+ et carbonate pour Z). 6(e) : le schéma est demandé à l'élève ; il est décrit dans le corrigé, aucune figure produite. 6(b)(ii) : le sujet imprime « SO3 2- » (sulfite) comme conclusion ; le précipité de sulfite de baryum se dissout dans l'acide, ce qui est cohérent.

En-tête de la Section A : « ANSWER ALL 5 questions. You will be graded for the best 4 answers » ; modélisé en « 4 sur 5 » (toutes tentées, 4 meilleures notées). Section B : « ANSWER ALL 2 questions » modélisé en « 2 sur 2 ». Section C : « ANSWER 2 QUESTIONS OUT OF 3 » (si plus de 2 tentées, seules les deux premières comptent) ; modélisé en « 2 sur 3 ».

questions.enonce_markdown:
Complete the conclusion for the tests on **X**.

(i) To 2 cm$^3$ of solution **X** is added 5 drops of $\mathrm{NaOH_{(aq)}}$ and warmed: a colourless pungent gas is evolved that turns damp red litmus paper blue. Conclusion: ......... *[2 marks]*

(ii) A sample of **X** is strongly heated in a test tube: a brown gas is evolved. Conclusion: ......... *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) The gas that turns damp red litmus blue and has a pungent smell is **ammonia, $\mathrm{NH_3}$**, so the **ammonium ion, $\mathrm{NH_4^+}$, is present**: $\mathrm{NH_4^+(aq)} + \mathrm{OH^-(aq)} \rightarrow \mathrm{NH_3(g)} + \mathrm{H_2O(l)}$.

(ii) The brown gas is **nitrogen dioxide, $\mathrm{NO_2}$**, so the **nitrate ion, $\mathrm{NO_3^-}$, is present** (X is a nitrate).

questions.enonce_markdown:
Complete the observations for the tests on **Y**.

(i) To 2 cm$^3$ of a solution of **Y**, is added 2 drops of $\mathrm{NaOH_{(aq)}}$. Observation: ......... Conclusion: $\mathrm{Fe^{2+}}$ ions present. *[1 mark]*

(ii) To 2 cm$^3$ of a solution of **Y**, is added 2 drops of $\mathrm{BaCl_{2(aq)}}$ followed by dil HCl. Observation: ......... Conclusion: $\mathrm{SO_3^{2-}}$ ions present. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **Observation:** a **dirty green precipitate** forms (iron(II) hydroxide, insoluble in excess NaOH): $\mathrm{Fe^{2+}(aq)} + 2\mathrm{OH^-(aq)} \rightarrow \mathrm{Fe(OH)_2(s)}$.

(ii) **Observation:** a **white precipitate** (barium sulphite) forms with $\mathrm{BaCl_2}$, and it **dissolves** when dilute HCl is added, with effervescence of a colourless gas with a choking smell ($\mathrm{SO_2}$): $\mathrm{Ba^{2+}(aq)} + \mathrm{SO_3^{2-}(aq)} \rightarrow \mathrm{BaSO_3(s)}$ then $\mathrm{BaSO_3(s)} + 2\mathrm{HCl(aq)} \rightarrow \mathrm{BaCl_2(aq)} + \mathrm{H_2O(l)} + \mathrm{SO_2(g)}$. (A sulphate would give a precipitate that does NOT dissolve.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
Complete the tests on **Z**.

(i) Test procedure: ......... Observation: **Z** gives a brick red flame colour. Conclusion: ......... *[3 marks]*

(ii) To 2 cm$^3$ of a solution of **Z**, is added 5 drops of dil HCl without heating: a gas is evolved which turns lime water milky. Conclusion: ......... *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **Test procedure (flame test):** clean a platinum or nichrome wire loop with concentrated HCl and heat it in a non-luminous Bunsen flame until it gives no colour. Dip the loop into the salt (moistened with concentrated HCl) and hold it in the edge of the flame; observe the colour. **Conclusion:** a brick red flame shows **calcium ions, $\mathrm{Ca^{2+}}$**, are present.

(ii) The gas that turns lime water milky is **carbon dioxide**, so **carbonate ions, $\mathrm{CO_3^{2-}}$, are present**: $\mathrm{CO_3^{2-}(aq)} + 2\mathrm{H^+(aq)} \rightarrow \mathrm{H_2O(l)} + \mathrm{CO_2(g)}$.

questions.enonce_markdown:
From the table identify X, Y and Z.

X .........

Y .........

Z ......... *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**X** contains $\mathrm{NH_4^+}$ and $\mathrm{NO_3^-}$: **ammonium nitrate, $\mathrm{NH_4NO_3}$**.

**Y** contains $\mathrm{Fe^{2+}}$ and $\mathrm{SO_3^{2-}}$: **iron(II) sulphite, $\mathrm{FeSO_3}$**.

**Z** contains $\mathrm{Ca^{2+}}$ and $\mathrm{CO_3^{2-}}$: **calcium carbonate, $\mathrm{CaCO_3}$**.

questions.enonce_markdown: To prepare and collect a dry sample of Ammonia gas in the laboratory, the following equipments and chemicals are provided: Round bottomed flask, delivery tubes, clamp and stand, drying tower, gas jar, solid $\mathrm{NH_4Cl}$, solid $\mathrm{Ca(OH)_2}$ and quicklime CaO. Draw and label the experimental set up you will use. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
*What to draw (left to right):*

1. A **round-bottomed flask** held by a clamp on a stand, slightly tilted downwards (so that water formed does not run back onto the hot glass), containing a **mixture of solid $\mathrm{NH_4Cl}$ and solid $\mathrm{Ca(OH)_2}$**, **heated** with a Bunsen burner. A delivery tube leaves the stopper.
2. A **drying tower** (or tube) packed with **quicklime, CaO**, which dries the gas. (Concentrated sulphuric acid and calcium chloride cannot be used because they react with ammonia.)
3. A **gas jar held upside down** (mouth downwards): the delivery tube goes up to the top of the jar. Ammonia is **less dense than air** and very soluble in water, so it is collected by **upward delivery (downward displacement of air)**.

Label: round-bottomed flask, $\mathrm{NH_4Cl} + \mathrm{Ca(OH)_2}$, heat, delivery tube, drying tower with CaO, gas jar, ammonia.

Equation: $2\mathrm{NH_4Cl(s)} + \mathrm{Ca(OH)_2(s)} \rightarrow \mathrm{CaCl_2(s)} + 2\mathrm{H_2O(l)} + 2\mathrm{NH_3(g)}$.
